Using only 18 cards, you'll draft and position sections of pier, building your unique structure outwards to sea in an effort to score the most victory points. During a player's turn they will draft one of the cards from the centre of the table and add this to their pier. This will make their pier larger but depending on how they place it can score them more or less points. The game ends when there are no cards left to draft and players tally up their in game (scoring the highest of that patron that round) and end gamepoints (a total of all icons scored) to determine who is the winner. Victory points are earned by meeting the needs of pier visitors and workers, as well as satisfying the demands of powerful patrons, who'll lend their support to one pier at the end of every round. You also choose a personal goal that you'll attempt to fulfill throughout the course of the game. After a number of rounds the player with the most victory points wins the game, and is crowned greatest pier builder of their generation! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Pier 18 is a two or three player game. There are 18 cards in the game. Start: Each player takes 3 cards and chooses their Plan card (objective) and Foundation card (ie. start of their Pier). First, each player decides which Plan they would like to keep from their 3 cards. If a player completes the objective on their Plan, they will score 4 points at the end of game. (note: on BGA this is the second card you will choose.) Second, each player selects a different card to be the Foundation of their Pier and places it face up, sideways on the left side of the table in front of them. The Foundation attaches to the land on the left and extends out to the water on the right. Third, each player selects their Plan card. This card also becomes the last card of their Pier at the end of the game. Place it face up on the right side of the table for reference. Each player then discards their remaining card. These are shuffled back into the deck. Play: In a two player game there are 4 rounds after placing the Foundations. A three player game has 3 rounds. The player with the earliest date (closest to January 1) on their Foundation card plays first in round 1. First player moves clockwise for each subsequent round. Each round, draw a number of cards face up equal to the number of players plus one. The first player chooses one card and adds it to their Pier. This card extends their Pier into the water and may overlap columns of the previous Pier card but cannot completely overlap it. Each choice will affect the scoring for each symbol on their Pier. Play continues clockwise with each player choosing one of the remaining cards and placing it on their Pier in the same way. The remaining card not selected becomes the Patron card for that round. In the top left of each card is a symbol which represents the Patron for that card. Each player counts up the number of points currently scoring for that symbol on their Pier (see scoring). The person with the most points for that symbol then receives the Patron card and places it face down on the left side of their Pier. In the event of a tie, the person who played the card with the earliest date for that round will receive the Patron. Patrons are worth 1 point each at the end of the game. Symbols are: Star - (Gold) Flower Seller Quill - (Blue) Poet Heart - (Red) Lovers Anchor - (Brown) Fisher A new round starts by drawing new cards face up. End of game: When there are not enough cards remaining to draw for a full round, each player places their Plan card as the final extension of their Pier. Each player does this at the same time and the game ends. Scoring: 1 point for every 2 Poets on their Pier. 2 points for each Lovers symbol with no other character within 2 spaces on the same side. [Rating: 3/10] Super quick card drafting game - for setup you determine your goal card and starting card, and then the game consists of drafting 4 cards, for each card deciding whether you will cover up 0-3 rows on your last played card.  There is also competition for a single Patron bonus point at the end of each round if you have the most icons that match the icons on the corner of the remaining non-drafted card - that seemed pretty random to me, but it was the deciding factor (everyone scored exactly 14 points + Patron points). [Rating: 4/10] This is a super-light drafting game that plays very quickly due to just having 18 cards and you only draft 6 cards each game. Like a lot of drafting games, it is a kind of set collection with individual goals. Have more Fishermen than Poets, that kind of thing.  I already have a surfeit of light drafting games and while this is pleasant enough I'm not sure it really does anything that would displace Sushi Go or Point Salad for me.

[Rating: 4/10] Microgames are always a little charming. Including this one! But only just-- it suffers the curse of the take-and-make: lots of options that add up to the same score, a false scarcity. The fact that you can't do everything makes decisions seem hard. But your opponent can't do everything either, and more to the point is constrained just as much as you are. It barely matters.

[Rating: 4/10] I think I am learning I just don't appreciate microgames like this. The way the game plays out it never feels like you have that much influence on... any of it... lol

[Rating: 4/10] I get why if tile laying is your favorite genre, you may like this more than I did. It's just not for me. (Rating based on digital play only)

[Rating: 4.018/10] Pier 18 is another of those 18 card micro-games. In general, I find micro games about as satisfying as eating a single M&M - you just never get enough. Plus, with many micro games, you wonder if you are playing the game or is the game playing you. That said, it’s a good design with an unusual theme and is nicely produced. Sure, it’s got a big dash of luck, but there are enough degrees of freedom to force you at times to have a meaningful think.
